title: FOIA Request: ADA Transition Plans and Complaints, South Loop, Chicago (Chicago Department of Transportation)

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Illinois Freedom of Information Act., I hereby request the following records:

Your agency's current ADA transition plan and any self-evaluation or progress report covering facilities your agency owns, operates, or maintains in the South Loop, defined as the area bounded by Congress Parkway to the north, Cermak Road to the south, Lake Michigan to the east, and the Chicago River to the west. These facilities may include curb ramps, sidewalks, pedestrian crossings, pedestrian signals, bridges and underpasses, and transit stations (including Roosevelt, Harrison, and Cermak-Chinatown). Please include the barriers identified, the deadlines set for removing them, and any records showing which barriers have been fixed and when, or which deadlines were missed or extended.

Additionally, all accessibility complaints, ADA grievances, service requests, and records of investigations or corrective action received or opened from January 1, 2025 to the present concerning the accessibility of those facilities in the area described above. This includes complaints about elevators, escalators, platforms, curb ramps, sidewalks, crosswalks, pedestrian signals, and bridges. For each, please include, if maintained: the date received, location, nature of the complaint, your agency's response, and the date of resolution. Personal identifying information of complainants may be redacted.

If your agency does not hold records for some of these facilities, please tell me which records you do not hold and, if known, which agency does. If any part of this request is unclear or burdensome, please contact me so we can narrow it. Please release records on a rolling basis rather than waiting to finish the entire request. If any records are withheld, please identify the specific exemption for each and the portion withheld, as required by 5 ILCS 140/9.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Luiselena Gutierrez Ubeda

title: ALPR Contract Terms, Licensed Products, Funding, and Data Deletion

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Texas Public Information Act, I hereby request the following records held by City Of Richardson related to agreements with any automated license plate reader (ALPR) or surveillance technology vendor (for example Flock Safety, Motorola Solutions, or Axon), from the start of the first such agreement to present:

1. All contracts, master service agreements, order forms, quotes, amendments, renewals, and terms of service, including any terms addressing data ownership, the vendor's rights to use, aggregate, or share data, data retention, data disposition upon termination, automatic renewal, termination, and price changes.
2. Records identifying every vendor product, feature, or service licensed or enabled, including but not limited to license plate readers, video cameras, drones, gunshot detection, investigative or AI-assisted search tools, and integrations with third-party camera networks.
3. Records showing the current contract term, expiration or renewal date, and the projected cost of renewal.
4. Grant applications, award letters, and grant agreements used to fund ALPR or related technology, including any conditions on use and the grant period.
5. Any notices received since August 1, 2026 from the Motor Vehicle Crime Prevention Authority, any other state agency, or any vendor regarding suspension of grant funding, payment pauses, contract changes, or removal of cameras.
6. Any certifications, attestations, or written confirmations from the vendor regarding deletion of data in accordance with the contract or the agency's retention policy.
7. Any vendor-provided usage, effectiveness, or return-on-investment reports.

This request covers records held by any city department, including the Richardson Police Department, as well as the City Secretary's Office, Purchasing, and Finance.

Please release all non-exempt portions and cite the specific statutory exception for anything withheld. If any item is unclear, please contact me for clarification rather than denying it.

I request records in their existing electronic format (such as native exports, CSV, or PDF) delivered by email or download link. I do not request paper copies, printouts, or physical media such as CDs or flash drives. I am not requesting that new reports be created. Please do not refer me to an online transparency portal in place of producing these records.

I request a waiver or reduction of fees, as release of this information primarily benefits the general public by informing residents about the use of surveillance technology in their community. If charges will exceed $40, please provide an itemized estimate, including any less costly alternative, before work begins.

Thank you for your cooperation. I look forward to your prompt response, as required by the Texas Public Information Act.

Sincerely,
Blackland Prairie Records Project

communications.subject: Texas Public Information Act Request: ALPR Search Audit Logs, 2025–Present
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Texas Public Information Act, I hereby request the following records held by The Colony Police Department concerning each automated license plate reader (ALPR) system it uses or has used since January 1, 2026, from any vendor (for example Flock Safety or Motorola Solutions). These records are generated within the ALPR systems, and standard system exports or screenshots of settings pages are sufficient. Where a record exists for more than one system, please provide it for each.

1. Search audit logs for each ALPR system from January 1, 2025 through the date this request is processed, showing searches by department users, including the user, date and time, and the reason or case number entered for each search (for example, the Flock Organization Audit report or the Motorola VehicleManager query audit).
2. Records of searches of the department's ALPR data by outside agencies from January 1, 2025 through the date this request is processed, including the searching agency, date and time, and the reason entered for each search (for example, the Flock Network Audit report).
3. Any records reflecting access to the department's cameras or data by vendor personnel (for example for product demonstrations, debugging, or support) from January 1, 2025 through the date this request is processed.
4. A copy of any script, macro, formula, or written procedure used to redact or replace plate numbers in the records released in response to items 1 and 2, and any record identifying the software used, excluding any key or mapping table that would allow placeholders to be matched back to plate numbers.
5. Drone flight logs from January 1, 2025 through the date this request is processed, including date, time, call type or purpose, and duration of each flight.

Redaction of plate numbers (items 1 and 2): Plate numbers that are confidential by law may be redacted. For any such redaction, I request that each plate number be replaced, consistently throughout the file, with a placeholder that cannot be used to recover the plate (for example, a randomly assigned code), so that repeated searches of the same plate remain distinguishable. This substitution can be applied programmatically to the entire export at once, and it is a method of redacting the existing records, not a request to create a new report. I do not agree to deletion of the plate column, or to blank or uniform redaction marks, in place of consistent placeholders. If the department believes consistent placeholders cannot be provided, please contact me before releasing these records.

These logs are exported from the system as files, so the length of the period should not materially change the time required. If the estimated charges for this request nonetheless exceed $40, please tell me before beginning work; I am willing to narrow the period, starting from the most recent months.

Please release all non-exempt portions and cite the specific statutory exception for anything withheld. If any item is unclear, please contact me for clarification rather than denying it.

I request records in their existing electronic format (such as native exports, CSV, or PDF) delivered by email or download link. I do not request paper copies, printouts, or physical media such as CDs or flash drives. I am not requesting that new reports be created. title: ALPR Policies, Sharing Settings, and System Configuration

communications.subject: Texas Public Information Act Request: ALPR Policies, Sharing Settings, and System Configuration
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Texas Public Information Act, I hereby request the following records held by The Colony Police Department concerning each automated license plate reader (ALPR) system it uses or has used since January 1, 2026, from any vendor (for example Flock Safety or Motorola Solutions). These records are generated within the ALPR systems, and standard system exports or screenshots of settings pages are sufficient. Where a record exists for more than one system, please provide it for each.

1. The department's current general order, directive, or written policy governing ALPR use, including operator access, the search-justification requirement, data retention, audit procedures, and data sharing.
2. For each ALPR system, the current data sharing settings, including:
   a. Agencies or networks sharing ALPR data with the department (in Flock, "shared with me");
   b. Agencies or networks the department shares its ALPR data with (in Flock, "networks I'm sharing");
   c. Any statewide, out-of-state, national, or federal sharing that is enabled, including sharing with the Texas Department of Public Safety and any access by federal agencies such as ICE, CBP, HSI, DEA, or DHS, with the date each such setting was enabled or disabled.
3. Records showing, for each ALPR system, the number of fixed, vehicle-mounted, and deployable or trailer-mounted cameras operated by or on behalf of the department, and the location of each fixed camera.
4. Records showing each ALPR system's configured data retention period and any changes to it since the start of the contract.
5. Records showing whether the department has access to commercially collected LPR data (for example data collected by private companies and made available through a vendor), and any agreement governing that access.
6. A list of non-government ALPR or video camera sources accessible to the department through any ALPR system (for example cameras owned by homeowners associations, businesses, apartment complexes, or residents), by owner type and general location.
7. Existing reports or exports from each ALPR system showing, by month since January 1, 2026: the number of alerts generated, the number of alerts confirmed by an officer, and the number of alerts determined to be misreads or false positives.
8. Any ALPR transparency reports or usage summaries prepared by or for the department since January 1, 2025.
9. Policies, directives, or standard operating procedures governing the department's other surveillance technologies, including live-feed and trailer-mounted cameras, 911 audio streaming, drones (including Drone as First Responder), and the Real-Time Intelligence Unit, including rules on access, retention, and sharing of video, audio, and images.
10. Records showing the configured retention periods for drone video, live-feed and trailer camera video, and 911 audio streams.

Please release all non-exempt portions and cite the specific statutory exception for anything withheld. If any item is unclear, please contact me for clarification rather than denying it.

I request records in their existing electronic format (such as native exports, CSV, or PDF) delivered by email or download link. I do not request paper copies, printouts, or physical media such as CDs or flash drives. I am not requesting that new reports be created. Please do not refer me to an online transparency portal in place of producing these records.

I request a waiver or reduction of fees, as release of this information primarily benefits the general public by informing residents about the use of surveillance technology in their community. If charges will exceed $40, please provide an itemized estimate, including any less costly alternative, before work begins.

Thank you for your cooperation. I look forward to your prompt response, as required by the Act.

Sincerely,

communications.communication:
Dear Blackland Prairie Records Project: 
Thank you for your interest in public records of Richardson Police Department. Your request has been received and is being processed in accordance with Chapter 552 of Texas Government Code, the Public Information Act. Your request was received in this office on 10/14/2026 and given the reference number P003444-101426 for tracking purposes. Records Requested: To Whom It May Concern: 

Pursuant to the Texas Public Information Act, I hereby request the following records held by Richardson Police Department concerning each automated license plate reader (ALPR) system it uses or has used since January 1, 2026, from any vendor (for example Flock Safety or Motorola Solutions). These records are generated within the ALPR systems, and standard system exports or screenshots of settings pages are sufficient. Where a record exists for more than one system, please provide it for each. 

1. Search audit logs for each ALPR system from January 1, 2025 through the date this request is processed, showing searches by department users, including the user, date and time, and the reason or case number entered for each search (for example, the Flock Organization Audit report or the Motorola VehicleManager query audit). 
2. Records of searches of the department's ALPR data by outside agencies from January 1, 2025 through the date this request is processed, including the searching agency, date and time, and the reason entered for each search (for example, the Flock Network Audit report). 
3. Any records reflecting access to the department's cameras or data by vendor personnel (for example for product demonstrations, debugging, or support) from January 1, 2025 through the date this request is processed. 
4. A copy of any script, macro, formula, or written procedure used to redact or replace plate numbers in the records released in response to items 1 and 2, and any record identifying the software used, excluding any key or mapping table that would allow placeholders to be matched back to plate numbers. 

Redaction of plate numbers (items 1 and 2): Plate numbers that are confidential by law may be redacted. For any such redaction, I request that each plate number be replaced, consistently throughout the file, with a placeholder that cannot be used to recover the plate (for example, a randomly assigned code), so that repeated searches of the same plate remain distinguishable. This substitution can be applied programmatically to the entire export at once, and it is a method of redacting the existing records, not a request to create a new report. I do not agree to deletion of the plate column, or to blank or uniform redaction marks, in place of consistent placeholders. If the department believes consistent placeholders cannot be provided, please contact me before releasing these records. 

These logs are exported from the system as files, so the length of the period should not materially change the time required. If the estimated charges for this request nonetheless exceed $40, please tell me before beginning work; I am willing to narrow the period, starting from the most recent months. 

Please release all non-exempt portions and cite the specific statutory exception for anything withheld. If any item is unclear, please contact me for clarification rather than denying it. 

I request records in their existing electronic format (such as native exports, CSV, or PDF) delivered by email or download link. title: ALPR Policies, Sharing Settings, and System Configuration

communications.communication:
